plain_description.what: On 14 MMLU-Pro anchors, it measured how reproducible each model's per-cell profile is across random halves of the questions. Overall model skill and cell difficulty were both removed first. The bar was 0.70. No calls were made.
plain_description.why: It tests whether a 'profile' is real per-cell information, or just the global score re-sorted by how hard each cell is.
plain_description.information: High reliability would mean profiles carry real per-cell strengths. Near-baseline reliability would mean they are just a global score. Result: done. The answer-key profile reliability is 0.87 [0.80, 0.93], so it passes. The judge-built profile is lower, at 0.67. The judge-built figures come from the older judged question family, later ruled 'history, not evidence'. A later disclosure noted that this tree had some evaluation questions leaking into its build; no number was changed.
